column1: # This file is the SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH: it is embedded in the binary (so the
# filter works with no database), and it seeds the junk_rules table on boot. The
# live filter is then loaded from that table into memory, so operators can add,
# tune, or disable rules without a code release.
# One rule per line so diffs are per-rule and a community PR adding a pattern
# reads as one line. Tab-separated. Lines starting with # are comments.
#   name    stable identifier, also what gets reported when a rule fires
#   rule    kind=regex: the pattern. kind=heuristic: the built-in algorithm id.
#   params  JSON object; {} when unused. Gates for regex rules, tuning for
# Order matters only for which name is reported first; the verdict is the same.
# Obfuscated posts use random-token subjects that would otherwise assemble into
# garbage "releases". Note that PATTERNS are what generalise here — a denylist of
# seen subjects is useless, because every obfuscated post is a fresh random

column5: 24+ consecutive alphanumerics anywhere = a hash or token. The workhorse rule.
A naked 16+ char run mixing upper and lower with NO separator. Real releases always carry a separator, so this catches the 16-23 char tokens that slip under long_alnum_run.
2+ segments (split on _ or space) of 5+ chars that each mix upper, lower AND digit. Real titles rarely do all three, almost never twice.
A canonical UUID as the release name.
Leftover poster-template tokens the poster never substituted: {total}, {{count}}.
Dot-separated obfuscated pair like f329yZ98AaYf2qHd.QPv2 — only when it mixes case AND digits, so real short names survive.
